searches.query: My rechargeable lantern battery has swollen. Should I use the usual ground return label to send it back?

chunks.text: Swollen, leaking, or damaged rechargeable batteries  Stop using or charging a rechargeable device if its battery swells, leaks, or is visibly damaged. Do not send it through the ordinary returns process. The store's regular ground return label is not an approved way to ship a damaged battery. Contact the product safety team through the support form and choose the battery-safety category.  Provide the product model, purchase reference, a description of the damage, and photographs when it is safe to take them. The team gives the customer instructions for the specific product and location. Support agents must not improvise a packaging method or tell customers to remove a swollen battery. Follow the device manufacturer's safety instructions while waiting for the team.  The general shipping article permits certain undamaged battery products to travel by ground. That permission does not apply to a damaged battery. Whether the item qualifies for a warranty remedy is assessed separately from how it can be handled safely.

Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service. A damaged, swollen, or leaking battery must never be sent using this ordinary label; use the damaged-battery procedure. Label creation does not count as dispatch. The parcel must actually be handed to the carrier within the return's dispatch deadline.

Tracking events come from the carrier after dispatch. Return transport for a device with a swollen, leaking, or damaged battery follows the damaged-battery procedure rather than the ordinary parcel-return process. Customers must not mail such a battery using an ordinary return label.

Check the condition, return window, gift status, and transport restrictions separately. A lantern that contains a lithium battery still follows the battery shipping rules. The recipient of an eligible gift return receives store credit under the gift policy; allocation does not change that credit into a bank-card refund. Original shipping fees and a purchased return label remain separate from these item amounts.

Who pays for a return label  For ordinary domestic change-of-mind returns, the store offers a ground label for USD 7 per parcel. If the customer uses it, USD 7 is deducted from the refund or store credit. A customer may instead arrange and pay for their own suitable carrier. A store label covers one parcel; two parcels require two labels. Membership does not waive this fee.  An approved wrong-item shipment or manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid label without the USD 7 deduction. The support team must approve that reason first. A customer selecting a defect reason in the portal is not sufficient proof that the claim has been approved. The hiking boot fit trial is a fit return, so the normal USD 7 label fee applies unless the customer supplies their own shipping.  Use suitable packaging and keep the carrier acceptance receipt. Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service.

Delivery restrictions for rechargeable products  Products containing lithium batteries travel by ground service within the contiguous United States. The rule covers rechargeable lanterns, headlamps, power banks, and navigation devices, including products whose batteries are installed inside the equipment. These products cannot be sent by our air services, to Alaska or Hawaii, or to an international destination.  Selecting express shipping at checkout does not override this restriction. If a mixed order includes an ordinary item and a rechargeable device, the rechargeable item still travels by ground. A support agent must not promise that paying the express surcharge makes a battery shipment eligible for air transport. The customer can remove the battery product and place a separate order for the other items if those items qualify for the requested service.  Ground shipping has the delivery estimate shown at checkout for the destination. This policy does not supply a guaranteed arrival date for a particular parcel. Tracking events come from the carrier after dispatch.

Reporting delivery damage or the wrong product  Report visible transport damage or a wrong product within seven calendar days after delivery. Keep the outer packaging and photograph the label, packing materials, and affected item. The support team compares those details with the shipment record before approving the claim. If the item is unsafe to use, stop using it while the report is assessed.  An approved wrong-product or delivery-damage return receives a prepaid label. The customer does not pay the ordinary USD 7 change-of-mind label fee for that approved return. The team confirms whether a replacement or another remedy will be provided. A report being opened does not prove replacement inventory exists or establish a delivery date for the replacement.  Damage involving a rechargeable battery follows the separate damaged-battery procedure. Do not put a leaking or swollen battery in an ordinary return parcel even when support is investigating delivery damage. A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process.

An international customer may use the return route if eligible and place a separate new order. Import taxes and international return transport are covered in the international-orders article. Exchange approval does not automatically waive a return-label fee.

The return-label fee follows the ordinary return-label policy. A recipient may use their own carrier if they do not want to buy the store label. This article does not describe the expiration date or transferability of store credit.

answer.answer: No, do not use the usual ground return label. A swollen battery must never be sent using the ordinary returns process or label. You should stop using the lantern immediately and contact the product safety team via the support form (selecting the battery-safety category) to receive specific instructions for your situation.
